experiment_name: Lifetime Inflation Experience: numeric versus qualitative

preregistered_evaluation.common_valid: same valid people across all three arms; report rates independently
preregistered_evaluation.aggregation: each repeat separately, equal-weight averages over four periods; survey weights auxiliary
preregistered_evaluation.age_groups: four selected per age group; descriptive only, no significance claim
preregistered_evaluation.bootstrap: paired people conditional on fixed P/E/history; 1000 draws, seed 42; not population or period generalization
preregistered_evaluation.repetition_rule: independent generations; repeat index is not a provider random seed
preregistered_evaluation.candidate_gate: same criterion versus original as well; no automatic production upgrade
preregistered_evaluation.truth_isolation: analysis only; official answers/weights not read during preparation or execution
preregistered_evaluation.representation_gate: both repeats: lower mean Q9 median error and W1 than numeric, both improve in >=3/4 periods

qualitative_duration_rule: observed complete spell >=12 months: extended; <=6: short-lived; middle: a while; left/right censoring explicitly retained
limitations: National history is a background proxy, not observed personal recall or residence history.
Era compression and retained information differ between common and matched arms; not a pure matching effect.
Start ages and 5% duration threshold are research conventions, not estimated universal thresholds.
Four previously studied periods remain development diagnostics; independent holdout not registered.
Current-byte history essays and previous news/gasoline limitations remain; not strict forecast B.
12-person age-balanced samples, four previously examined periods, no independent holdout.
All existing confidence/CE/news assumptions retained; no new shopping weights or probability reporting instructions.
No own prior answers, panel memory, core/normal expansion or social interaction.
Equal count in three age groups is not a nationally representative age distribution.
Historical context and compression differ between common and age-matched arms; not a pure matching causal effect.
Qualitative history also shortens context and removes exact age/month/rate details; not pure isolation of CPI digits.
